findings.evidence: `ConditionallyIIDWithFamily.jointLaw_eq_disintegration` at line 118 gives the same right-hand side for every injective selection, while `ExchangeableFamily.blockLaw_eq` at line 68 is the required conclusion; `rg -n "exchangeable.*conditionallyIID|conditionallyIID.*exchangeable|ExchangeableFamily"` finds no family implication.
findings.fix: Add `ConditionallyIIDWithFamily.exchangeableFamily` by equating both selected block laws through their common disintegration, and the parallel `ConditionallyIIDFamily.exchangeableFamily` obtained from its directing witness.
findings.issue: Neither `ConditionallyIIDWithFamily` nor its existential wrapper exposes that a conditionally i.i.d. family is `ExchangeableFamily`, forcing consumers to reconstruct the defining block-law argument.

summary: The family API omits the basic implication from conditional i.i.d.-ness to exchangeability, so the new predicates do not provide the interaction needed to use the theorem as a de Finetti characterization.
